title: Concept 44. Duplicate Work Across Agents
summary: Duplicate work occurs when multiple agents perform the same task unnecessarily.

sections.title: 1. What is duplicate work?
sections.body:
(Resource wastage problem)

Duplicate work occurs when multiple agents perform the same task unnecessarily.

It wastes:

- Tokens.
- API calls.
- Execution time.
- Money.
- Compute resources.

It can also cause duplicate side effects.

scenario.title: Scenario — Concept 44. Duplicate Work Across Agents
scenario.situation: User asks: Compare the latest three LLM providers. Supervisor delegates: - Agent 1: Research OpenAI. - Agent 2: Research Anthropic. - Agent 3: Research Google. But Agent 1 and Agent 2 both research OpenAI. The system wastes resources and may generate duplicate information.

choices.label: Ignore it and ship anyway
choices.explanation: Skipping detection leaves users exposed and makes root-cause analysis harder later.

choices.label: Add detection signals first
choices.explanation: - Track task IDs. - Compare task descriptions. - Detect repeated API requests. - Monitor duplicate tool calls. - Track cost per completed task. - Compare agent execution traces. - Identify overlapping task ownership.

choices.label: Apply a production fix / mitigation
choices.explanation: Apply layered mitigations, validate with tests, and monitor recovery.

sections.title: 2. Why does it happen?
sections.body:
- No shared task registry.
- No task ownership.
- Poor task decomposition.
- Supervisor assigns overlapping tasks.
- Agents cannot see completed work.
- Retry mechanisms create duplicate jobs.
- Parallel execution lacks deduplication.

sections.title: 4. Real-time example
sections.body:

Supervisor delegates:

But Agent 1 and Agent 2 both research OpenAI.

The system wastes resources and may generate duplicate information.

sections.title: 5. How to detect it?
sections.body:
- Track task IDs.
- Compare task descriptions.
- Detect repeated API requests.
- Monitor duplicate tool calls.
- Track cost per completed task.
- Compare agent execution traces.
- Identify overlapping task ownership.

sections.title: 6. How to fix it?
sections.body:
**Solution 1 — Task registry**

Maintain a central record of all tasks and their owners.

```python
task_registry = {
    "task_101": {
        "description": "Research OpenAI",
        "assigned_to": "agent_1",
        "status": "completed"
    },
    "task_102": {
        "description": "Research Anthropic",
        "assigned_to": "agent_2",
        "status": "running"
    }
}
```

**Solution 2 — Task ownership**

Each task should have one clearly defined owner unless intentional collaboration is required.

**Solution 3 — Deduplication**

Use task fingerprints or unique IDs to prevent accidental duplicate submissions.

**Solution 4 — Shared results**

Store completed task outputs so other agents can reuse them.

**Solution 5 — Cost controls**

Set per-task and per-workflow budgets.

**Memory trick:**

> Duplicate work = Multiple agents do the same job unnecessarily.
